session_note: Oklahoma's 60th Legislature runs a two-year biennium (2025-2026) but each year's session adjourns sine die separately; 2025 bills not enacted by the 2025 sine die date generally remain alive and can be taken up again in the 2026 session of the same 60th Legislature (as SB 259 was, carried from its 2025-02-03 introduction through to 2026 passage). The Second Regular Session of the 60th Oklahoma Legislature convened 2026-02-02 and adjourned sine die on Friday, 2026-05-29 (NLT 5:00 p.m.), per the official House legislative deadlines page (okhouse.gov/leg_deadlines). Any bill not passed and signed into law by that date is dead for the 2025-2026 biennium; a new bill number would be required starting with the 2027 session.

fields.key_provisions: Data Center Customer (Ratepayer) Protection Act of 2026. Requires large-load users (data centers, AI facilities, crypto mining) to pay their share of electric/infrastructure costs and carry separate billing terms; final version went to a House-Senate conference committee (adopted 2026-05-04/05) which reconciled the House and Senate-amended versions (60-day notice, nearby-landowner and newspaper notice, public meeting, noncompliance fines) before both chambers passed the conference report and it was enrolled, signed, and sent to the Governor.

fields.key_provisions: Groundwater metering/permitting bill (originally introduced 2025-02-03, carried into the 2026 session of the same 60th Legislature), amended by committee substitute in both chambers to prohibit groundwater cooling at a data processing facility or data center through open-air evaporative or other consumptive cooling, unless OWRB determines the system uses closed-loop, dielectric immersion, or comparably low-consumptive technology. Passed Senate 36-11 (2026-03-25), passed House as amended 88-1 (2026-05-06), House amendments adopted by Senate 38-10 (2026-05-14), sent to Governor same day, approved 2026-05-20.
